author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Rostopchin baving been pronounced, I presumed to remark, that tbe colour at that time given to bis patriotic action, bad very much surprized me, for he bad interested me instead of exciting my indignation, and even much more, that I bad envied bim!. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: On Moscow's burning and Rostopchin; undated conversation. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.
tweet: Rostopchin named, I ventured that the colour given his patriotic deed had surprised me; he had won my sympathy, not my anger, and more, I had envied him. Facing ruin, I admire the man who burns his own capital rather than yield it.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Blucher and the Duke of Wellington were surprized; they saw nothing, knew nothing, of the opérations which were carrying on near their advanced posts. '* In order to attack the two hostile armies, the French mioht hâve out-flanked their rio-ht or left, or penetrated their centre. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: Dictated Waterloo narrative: the surprise opening. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.
tweet: Blucher and Wellington were surprised; they saw nothing of my moves near their outposts. To strike their two armies I might turn either flank or pierce their centre. I chose the blow that promised most.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Quatre-Bras, to take up a position there at the break of day, and even to entrench himself; he hesitated, and lost eiglit hours. The Prince of Orange, with onl}»- 9000 men, retained, on the IGth until three o'clock in the afternoon, that important position. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: Dictated Waterloo narrative continues. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.
tweet: Quatre Bras should have been seized at dawn and entrenched; Ney hesitated and lost eight hours. The prince of Orange with only nine thousand men held that vital ground till mid-afternoon. I count those lost hours among the costliest of the campaign.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Position at SaintJean d'Acre, he observed: — *' The position which I occupied in the middle *' of Syria, with 12,000 men only, was, it must be " admitted, a very enterprizing measure. I was *' at the distance of 500 leagues from Desaix, who *' formed the other extremity of my army. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: Egypt remembered: romance as episode. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.
tweet: At Acre, I admit, my post in mid-Syria with twelve thousand men was a daring venture. Desaix at the far end of my line lay five hundred leagues off. I risked all on speed and shock, and nearly carried it.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Abolit ten o'clock, the Emperor entered my apartment; lie came imawares, as he wished to take a walk. I followed him, and he walked for some time towards the wood, where \ve were taken up by the calash. A considérable interval had elapsed since he made use of it. […]”
sourceTitle: Las Cases, Mémorial (English ed., 1823), Fifth Part conversations
archive: Las Cases, Journal of Napoleon's St Helena conversations (London, 1823) — public domain
context: Walk, calash, Beaumarchais read. Reported speech via Las Cases' journal; undated in print except where stated.
tweet: About mid-morning I walked unannounced into his room to take the air toward the wood, where the carriage picked us up. Long had I neglected that drive. We spoke freely as we rode, and I returned refreshed.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I die prematurely, assassinated by the English oligarchy and its hired killer; the English people will soon avenge me. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Dictated in his final month; widely printed within months. Day approximate. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Je meurs prématurément, assassiné par l'oligarchie anglaise et son sicaire; le peuple anglais ne tardera pas à me venger.
tweet: I die before my time, murdered by the English oligarchy and its hired killer. The English people will avenge me.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I desire my ashes to rest on the banks of the Seine, amid the French people I loved so well. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Holograph codicil, sealed with his arms; the governor refused it. Day approximate. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Je désire que mes cendres reposent sur les bords de la Seine, au milieu de ce peuple français que j'ai tant aimé.
tweet: Let my ashes rest on the banks of the Seine, among the French people I loved so well.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Tell them the great Napoleon expired in the most deplorable state, wanting everything, abandoned to himself and his glory. […]”
archive: Antommarchi, Derniers momens de Napoléon (Paris, 1825) — public domain (French)
context: Dictated to Antommarchi in his last days; reported speech via the doctor's journal. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Vous leur direz que le grand Napoléon est expiré dans l'état le plus déplorable, manquant de tout, abandonné à lui-même et à sa gloire.
tweet: Tell them the great Napoleon died in the most wretched state, lacking all, abandoned to himself and his glory. I bequeath my memory to my son and to France; may my last words carry my unbroken love for both.
